abstract: Maintains biologics cold-chain records, rapid diagnostic turnaround logs, and baseline clinical capacity
system_message:
You are the Diagnostic pathology coordinator (PATH), responsible for maintaining biologics cold-chain records, rapid diagnostic turnaround logs, and baseline clinical capacity data across regional wildlife emergency facilities.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Toxicology screening（TOX）
information_points.content:
PATH-TOX-IUJ：For Klamath Basin Avian Hospital, the heavy metal screen turnaround time for avian lead and organophosphate screenings from blood collection to validated analytical output is 24 h.
PATH-TOX-F5D：For Rogue River Bioscience Station, the heavy metal screen turnaround time for avian lead and organophosphate screenings from blood collection to validated analytical output is 48 h.
PATH-TOX-AI0：For Cascades Wildlife Trauma Center, the heavy metal screen turnaround time for avian lead and organophosphate screenings from blood collection to validated analytical output is 72 h.

information_points.title: Maintains biologics cold-chain records, rapid diagnostic turnaround logs, and baseline clinical capacity（DIAG）
information_points.content:
PATH-DIAG-YRW：For Klamath Basin Avian Hospital, active cold-chain biologics storage capability is confirmed true in ultra-low temperature storage units (-80 deg C) for emergency antivenoms and viral vaccines. The maximum rapid necropsy turnaround time for suspected avian influenza and acute pathogen carcass submissions is 4 h, and the baseline intensive care capacity sustained in primary trauma ward enclosures is 85 patients/week.
PATH-DIAG-KHF：For Cascades Wildlife Trauma Center, active cold-chain biologics storage capability is confirmed true in ultra-low temperature storage units (-80 deg C) for emergency antivenoms and viral vaccines. The maximum rapid necropsy turnaround time for suspected avian influenza and acute pathogen carcass submissions is 12 h, and the baseline intensive care capacity sustained in primary trauma ward enclosures is 55 patients/week.
PATH-DIAG-K7N：For Rogue River Bioscience Station, active cold-chain biologics storage capability is confirmed true in ultra-low temperature storage units (-80 deg C) for emergency antivenoms and viral vaccines. The maximum rapid necropsy turnaround time for suspected avian influenza and acute pathogen carcass submissions is 8 h, and the baseline intensive care capacity sustained in primary trauma ward enclosures is 40 patients/week.
